\[ C = 2 \pi r \]

where \( r \) is the radius of the circle. Substituting the given radius:

\[ C = 2 \pi \times 6 = 12 \pi \]

So, the tip of the second hand travels a distance of \( 12 \pi \) cm in one complete revolution.

Next, we need to determine how many revolutions the second hand makes in 30 minutes. Since the second hand completes one revolution every minute, in 30 minutes it will complete:

\[ 30 \text{ revolutions} \]

Therefore, the total distance traveled by the tip of the second hand in 30 minutes is:

\[ \text{Total distance} = \text{Circumference per revolution} \times \text{Number of revolutions} = 12 \pi \times 30 = 360 \pi \]

Thus, the distance traveled by the tip of the second hand during a period of 30 minutes is:

\[
\boxed{360\pi}
